results.summary: This design is a multiply-accumulate unit that operates on 8-bit posit numbers rather than standard floating-point or integer formats. It accepts 8-bit feature data and a 2-bit command input while exposing ready, busy, prediction-valid, model-loaded and error status outputs. The design produces an 8-bit prediction and supports loading a model through its command interface. It is controlled through a simple valid/ready handshake with separate command bits.

This design generates a perfect 10x10 maze on-chip using a binary-tree algorithm and displays it over VGA while it is being built. The maze is rendered graphically on a VGA display, and the construction process is visible in real time. The design uses a gamepad or PS2 input for interaction, and the maze can be navigated as a puzzle. The project is implemented in Verilog and targets FPGA platforms.

This design is a counter that can be controlled and monitored through a UART interface. It includes a sensor interface for external input, and the counter value can be read or set via serial commands. The design is intended for use as a simple measurement or timing tool. It is implemented in Verilog and verified with a cocotb testbench.

This design generates a VGA video signal that displays a graphical pattern or artwork. It uses a signal generator to produce the video timing and pixel data, and the output is intended for artistic or demoscene purposes. The design is also suitable for educational demonstrations of video generation. It is implemented in Verilog and targets FPGA platforms.

This design implements a Pong-style arcade game with VGA output and button inputs. The game uses a debouncer for the button inputs and renders the game graphics on a VGA display. It is designed for FPGA platforms and is intended for interactive play. The project is a classic game implementation suitable for educational purposes.

This design is a multiply-accumulate unit that operates on 8-bit posit numbers rather than standard floating-point or integer formats. It accepts 8-bit feature data and a 2-bit command input while exposing ready, busy, prediction-valid, model-loaded and error status outputs. The design produces an 8-bit prediction and supports loading a model through its command interface. It is controlled through a simple valid/ready handshake with separate command bits.

This design provides eight PWM outputs that are exposed on the output pins, and a UART input on a bidirectional pin. The PWM outputs can be used to control LEDs or other devices, and the UART interface allows external control of the PWM duty cycles. The design is implemented in Verilog and is suitable for educational or hobbyist projects. It is a simple and flexible PWM generator with serial control.

This design implements a small translation lookaside buffer acting as a memory management unit for a TTL logic chip breadboard CPU. The TLB is intended to sit alongside a discrete CPU and provides address translation for memory accesses. The design targets latch-based memory and is implemented in SystemVerilog. It is a memory management unit for a breadboard CPU.

This design generates a VGA video signal that displays a graphical pattern or artwork. It uses a signal generator to produce the video timing and pixel data, and the output is intended for artistic or demoscene purposes. The design is also suitable for educational demonstrations of video generation. It is implemented in Verilog and targets FPGA platforms.

This design is a compact RISC-V RV32I CPU that uses external QSPI PSRAM or flash as its program and data memory, implemented as a state machine for Tiny Tapeout. It includes a 64-bit free-running counter with interrupt, a QSPI memory interface, 4-bit GPIO, 3-bit GPO, 6-bit GPI, one interrupt pin and a UART monitor with commands for memory read/write, breakpoints, register access and execution. Testing requires an external QSPI PSRAM and a UART terminal to upload and run programs. The design is a full CPU with memory and I/O interfaces.
